current_literal_proofs.quote:
15.Mazor M, Moran R, Fleming SM. 2021. 
Metacognitive asymmetries in visual perception. Neurosci. Conscious.
2021, niab025. ( 10.1093/nc/niab025)

Previous studies found that this alignment, commonly referred to as metacognitive sensitivity, is reduced for decisions about target absence compared with decisions about target presence [6,10,15,16]. Here also, metacognitive sensitivity (quantified as the area under the response-conditional type-II receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve) was significantly higher for detection ‘yes’ compared with ‘no’ responses (t34 = 6.41, p < 0.001, d = 1.1; figure 2c).

decisions.reason: Parent independently read current Mazor/Gong/Fleming2023Results2.1and reference15, and newly recovered complete publisher Stage2Mazor/Moran/Fleming2021niab025ResultsExperiment7andDiscussion. Current new35included participants directly compare response-conditional auROC2 for gratingpresence versus absence; current explicitly attributes the corresponding published asymmetry to ref15and reports the same direction. The2021original positive-controlExperiment7reports presence/absence auROC2.75/.68with both raw and adjusted asymmetry, distinct from its six preregistered discrimination experiments and from the2020eLife neural study. Current null clockwise/anticlockwise result also agrees with the relevant discrimination contrast; novel tilt recognition is not attributed as an original2021endpoint. Do not transfer the separate2020neural mixed findings or aggregate unrelated2021stimulus-pair outcomes into this actual behavioural comparison. The prior final scope transport failed twice; all spent attempts/objections remain, but newly acquired complete original supplies the previously absent original-specific evidence. This is an obvious direct finding-to-finding comparison under codebook rules, not a third unchanged model call. Keep shipped9792021original; separate2020neural missingpair remains genuinely distinct.
